t.E331.agn: JECFA included sodium citrates in the citric acid group ADI ('not limited'); it noted that sodium citrate has been used in medicine for many years at doses of up to 10 g per day.
t.E331.body: Citric acid and citrates are normal intermediates of the tricarboxylic acid (Krebs) cycle, which produces energy in the body.
t.E331.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E331.found.1: Infant formulae and complementary foods for infants (in the EU only under limited conditions such as pH adjustment)
t.E331.prod: Obtained by neutralising citric acid with sodium hydroxide or sodium carbonate.
t.E331.pw.0: It is a source of sodium. Sodium from additives is mostly lower than from salt.
t.E331.regx.0: ADI 'not limited'; included in the citric acid group ADI.
t.E331.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E331.regx.2: Permitted under limited conditions in infant formulae and complementary foods for infants (maximum 2000 mg/kg in infant formulae).
t.E331.summary: The sodium salts of citric acid. They regulate acidity; used as emulsifying salts in processed cheese and to soften sourness in drinks.
t.E331.what: The sodium salts of citric acid, used as acidity regulators, buffers and stabilisers.
